title: Juniper and the Ember
premise: Paloma Coldharbour, a debt-bound temple scribe with a hidden gift for reading the true names of things, keeps ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Trades. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, he shelters Juniper, a feral child whose ember-gift burns brighter than any the Guild has catalogued. Together they discover that King Aldous died years ago and the thing wearing his crown feeds on gifted souls to stay animate. To unbind the kingdom, Paloma must sacrifice his own name — the last anchor of his identity — while Juniper must choose between becoming the new vessel of the ember or letting it die. In the end, the found family they've gathered breaks the crown's hunger, Paloma rewrites his name from memory of love rather than law, and Juniper tames the ember into something small enough to carry.
about_author: F. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate ledgers before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people caught between them from a drafty house full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He balances impossible accounts at the Guild of Impossible Trades, hiding the tremor in his hands when ink moves on its own. Establishes his debt-bond to the temple and his careful, invisible life. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A ledger entry writes itself in his hand — a warning he didn't pen. His mentor Brother Cassian notices and says nothing, but Paloma knows his secret is fraying. Emotional beat: fear of being seen.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Criers announce the Crown's hunt for the gifted; bells toll across Coldharbour. The Guild quietly begins selling names of suspected gift-bearers. Emotional beat: the world tilting.

chapters.title: A Girl in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He finds Juniper, a soot-streaked child, hiding among the archive shelves, pursued by Guild catchers. Her touch makes candle flames bow toward her. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition of himself in her.

chapters.title: Terms of Shelter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He bargains with Guild mistress Veyra to hide Juniper as 'inventory' pending appraisal, buying time at terrible interest. Emotional beat: guilt dressed up as cleverness.

chapters.title: What the Ember Wants
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, first time. Through her eyes we see the ember inside her as a hungry, lonely warmth that whispers promises. She doesn't trust Paloma yet. Emotional beat: loneliness meeting cautious hope.

chapters.title: The Appraiser Comes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A crown appraiser arrives to inspect the Guild's stock. Paloma falsifies entries using his true-name gift for the first time in years, and it costs him a memory he can't identify. Emotional beat: the price of the gift made literal.

chapters.title: Brother Cassian's Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cassian reveals he has known about Paloma's gift since novitiate and has been erasing his name from temple reports for years. Emotional beat: found family's first root.

chapters.title: The King's Face
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At a public audience, Paloma glimpses King Aldous and his gift reads the truth: nothing behind the eyes but appetite wearing a man's shape. Emotional beat: horror and certainty.

chapters.title: Veyra's Price
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Veyra offers to smuggle them out of the city — if Paloma appraises the crown itself for the Guild. He accepts before understanding what it means. Emotional beat: ambition and trap entwined.

chapters.title: Running the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma and Juniper flee through the salt marshes with catchers behind them; Juniper's ember flares and nearly betrays them. They argue, then bond over stolen plums. Emotional beat: trust kindling.

chapters.title: The Hollow Chapel
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They shelter in a ruined chapel where Paloma's gift shows him echoes of an old rite: the Binding of the Crown, performed by three names together. Emotional beat: a map hidden in grief.

chapters.title: Tallow and Thorn
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper meets Wren, a one-handed tinker who feeds them and asks no questions, then follows anyway. Found family grows by one. Emotional beat: being chosen without conditions.

chapters.title: The Catcher's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she was once a catcher and still carries the list of the taken; her sister's name is on it. She joins not for Juniper but for the dead. Emotional beat: grief converted to purpose.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Veyra's men catch up; she demands the crown-appraisal now, revealing the Guild plans to sell the binding rite to the highest bidder. Paloma realizes he's collateral. Emotional beat: betrayal by the transactional world.

chapters.title: Names Are Debts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a night conversation with Juniper, Paloma explains how his debt-bound name keeps him owned — and how the rite will demand a freely given name. Emotional beat: theme crystallized: identity as currency versus identity as self.

chapters.title: The City of Bells
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The company infiltrates the capital during the Feast of Bells, disguised as Guild porters. Juniper sees wealth and waste for the first time. Emotional beat: wonder sharpened by anger.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma reads the crown itself and recoils: it is a mouth, patient and old, and it has already tasted him once — the missing memory. Emotional beat: violation and resolve.

chapters.title: What Aldous Was
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV (letters). Interleaved letters reveal King Aldous bound the crown willingly decades ago to end a famine, trading his soul for his people's bread. Emotional beat: tragic symmetry with Paloma's choice.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Waits
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They find Queen Isolde, alive, sequestered, and complicit — she has kept the king fed with condemned prisoners to buy reform time. Emotional beat: love against duty, darkened.

chapters.title: Juniper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The ember offers Juniper a deal: give herself fully and no one else need burn. She almost says yes. Paloma interrupts. Emotional beat: temptation of self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Veyra sells them out to the crown. Wren is taken; Cassian is killed covering their escape. Emotional beat: devastating midpoint loss.

chapters.title: Ashes and Interest
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Grieving, Paloma wants to trade himself to the crown directly. Juniper refuses to let him, calling him family in plain words for the first time. Emotional beat: love as refusal.

chapters.title: The Rite Requires Three
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde's POV. She explains the Binding needs three willing names: one to hold, one to speak, one to burn. She intends to be all three. Emotional beat: duty curdled into martyrdom.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The company raids the palace undercroft where the taken are held; they free Wren and dozens of others. Juniper's ember answers the captives' gifts like calls to like. Emotional beat: fury turned to rescue.

chapters.title: The Mouth Opens
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The crown, sensing the rite's components gathering, begins feeding openly; the king's body starts to fail in public. Riots spark. Emotional beat: clock running down.

chapters.title: Veyra's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma confronts Veyra and wins — not by force but by reading her own true name aloud, showing her the girl she was before the Guild. She lets them go. Emotional beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: One to Hold
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The company chooses roles for the rite. Wren claims 'to hold,' anchoring the working with her sister's name. Emotional beat: chosen purpose replacing lost family.

chapters.title: One to Speak
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma must speak the unbinding — which means surrendering his name entirely, becoming unwritten. He spends a last evening memorizing his friends' faces instead of words. Emotional beat: farewell without goodbye.

chapters.title: One to Burn
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Everyone assumes Juniper must burn. Instead she proposes the ember take the crown's place — fed willingly, in balance, never starving. Emotional beat: rewriting the terms of destiny.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV vignettes. Quiet chapter: mended clothes, shared bread, Wren carving a wooden bird, Isolde writing an abdication. Emotional beat: tenderness before the storm.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the throne room, the rite begins. Wren holds, Paloma speaks, and the crown fights back with every memory it has eaten, drowning him in borrowed lives. Emotional beat: climax, part one.

chapters.title: The Nameless Scribe
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Paloma's name unravels mid-rite; he forgets why he's speaking but keeps speaking because Juniper's voice anchors him. The crown loosens. Emotional beat: love holding identity's place.

chapters.title: What the Crown Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The unbinding completes; Aldous's remnant surfaces for one lucid minute, thanks them, and ends. The crown falls silent — but the ember must go somewhere now. Emotional beat: grief and awe.

chapters.title: The New Vessel Question
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The council of survivors debates: destroy the ember and lose the gifts forever, or crown it in Juniper's plan. Isolde argues for destruction; Juniper argues for trust. Emotional beat: the thematic argument staged honestly.

chapters.title: Ember, Tamed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper takes the ember not into her body but into the wooden bird Wren carved, making it small, portable, and shared — a hearth, not a hunger. Emotional beat: triumph through reframing.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Nameless, Paloma discovers he can write himself anew — and chooses a name given by his friends rather than the temple. He signs the Guild's ledgers closed forever. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed as authorship.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde abdicates; a regency council including Wren and Veyra reforms the succession, and the hunt for the gifted is formally ended with reparations. Emotional beat: institutions bending toward justice.

chapters.title: Hearthlight
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue. One year later: the company shares a house above a rebuilt chapel; Juniper teaches gifted children; Paloma writes stories under a name that is truly his. The ember glows gently on the mantel. Emotional beat: home, earned.
